body.statement: Under sequential randomization, overlap, bounded outcomes, bounded aspect ratio, propensity-path stability, and \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), \(\max_{i\in I}|\widehat p_i-\bar p_i|=O_P(\sqrt{\log(en)/m})\) and \(\lVert D^{\mathrm B}\rVert/\lambda_{nm}=O_P(Bq^{-2}\sqrt{n\log(en)}/\lambda_{nm})=O_P(b_{nm})=o_P(1)\). If the primitive oracle gap holds, then \(P\{\sigma_r(T^{\mathrm B})-\sigma_{r+1}(T^{\mathrm B})\ge(c_{\mathrm B}/2)\lambda_{nm}\}\to1\).
body.justification: This derives the realized tangent gap from a primitive oracle gap and path concentration instead of assuming a property of the random normalized target.
body.gap: Cai et al. perturb a fixed signal under independent entries, while Khan and Ugander linearize scalar ratios; neither transfers an oracle singular gap through a same-path adaptive row denominator.
body.consumer: It supplies a checkable sufficient condition for stable blind SVD in archived experiments.
